summary: Browser back-navigation (bfcache) leaves zombie SSE session on edge and prevents finalization of stream
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when an end user navigates back using the browser back button (hit bfcache/back-forward cache) during a long SSE streaming response, the stream on the server/edge remains open but the finalization (end event/EOF metadata) is not applied to the customer's resumed session. Impact:
- End user sees partial output and no terminal 'done' event; UI remains stuck waiting for finalization.
- Metrics show server-side stream kept alive and not garbage-collected because edge shows client still connected.
Environment:
- Customer app: CloudMuse web app (React, single-page app).
- SDK: web-js v0.9.4 using EventSource polyfill + our reconnect helper.
- CDN/edge: FastEdge (customer uses our recommended CDN config).
- Affected region: us-east (reported).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a long streaming generation (20–40s).
2) While streaming, use the browser back button to go to previous route (SPA uses history.back; page kept in bfcache).
3) Return to the page using forward navigation (restores from bfcache).
4) Initiate another stream or rely on SDK reconnect.

Expected behavior:
- Previous SSE session should be fully closed, server should receive indication that client detached, and a fresh session should be established when navigating back.
- Final 'end' metadata from the original stream should either have been delivered before bfcache or server should garbage-collect quickly and not block subsequent sessions.

Actual behavior:
- Edge retains a socket tied to original client-id; server-side runtime keeps KV/cache and does not emit final event to the restored client.
- New session gets a different client-id but service-side routing avoids duplicate final events; UI never receives terminal marker and the conversation is stuck in 'streaming' state.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Chrome 112+ (or Firefox with bfcache enabled) on a React SPA. 2) Start a long SSE stream. 3) Do browser back (page is placed into bfcache). 4) Wait ~5–30s, then forward navigate to restore the page. 5) Observe that finalization for the prior stream is not delivered and the new session waits for a terminal event.
logs_and_repro_artifacts:
Customer provided: client-side debug logs, EVENTSOURCE frames with timestamps, FastEdge connection logs (edge-session-id: FE-zz-99321), and support-app trace id: trace-20260310-CLM-55. Excerpt (edge logs):
[2026-03-10T16:12:05Z] FE-zz-99321: Accept incoming SSE connection client-id=cust-7f3
[2026-03-10T16:12:28Z] FE-zz-99321: HTTP/2 PING from origin during bfcache pause; no FIN from client
[2026-03-10T16:13:00Z] FE-zz-99321: connection still active (no client socket close)
Server runtime trace:
[stream-runtime] stream-id=sr-20411 retained due to active kv-handle; last-emitted-token-index=128; terminal-flag=false
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: bfcache restores the DOM without closing the browser's TCP/socket at the same time edge/CDN keeps connection open; our runtime uses client-id binding and expects explicit close or idle timeout to finalize. Because the edge keeps the connection optimized for long-lived connections, server never receives expected disconnect.
Engine hypotheses considered:
- Edge keeps upstream connection open even though client is logically swapped (bfcache) and client-side polyfill does not send an SSE close.
- Our reconnect helper uses a new client-id on restore; server-side routing detects mismatch and does not replay terminal event into the new session to avoid duplicate delivery.
- Idle/GC thresholds are too long when there is an active edge session, so stream stays alive beyond reasonable user expectation.

Findings so far:
- Reproduced internally with Chrome when enabling bfcache using a local SPA test harness.
- When FastEdge 'probe' or http/2 PING occurs during bfcache, the edge does not surface immediate close to origin.
- Server logs show the stream runtime preserved state and no 'client-detach' event for ~60s, after which idle timer GC kicked in and a terminal event emitted — too late for the user's immediate UX.
customer_communication_summary:
2026-03-10: Customer reported issue and supplied logs and repro steps.
2026-03-11: Support reproduced internally and requested permission to run a packet capture with the customer's consent (customer approved).
2026-03-12: Engineering triaged and requested additional FastEdge logs (we asked customer to request CDN support case).
comments: Maya Chen (Support): Thanks for the detailed repro. We can reproduce with Chrome bfcache. Working with Eng to determine whether we should close sessions on DOM hidden/visibilitychange events.
Diego Alvarez (SRE): Reproduced locally. Edge keeps upstream alive on bfcache. Short-term: lower idle GC for streams with SDK-js client-id patterns to 10s for this customer as a targeted mitigation.

CloudMuse Engineer (customer): We prefer a server-side change rather than changing client behaviour; we'll coordinate with FastEdge to see if they can surface a connection close when browser bfcache engages.
temporary_workaround: 1) Upgrade SDK-js to v0.9.5 (hotfix) which sends an explicit 'sse:close' event on visibilitychange if the page is going into bfcache/back-forward cache. 2) On server, enable targeted reduced idle-GC for streams from this customer to 10s while we root-cause.
long_term_fix_plan:
- Engineering to add server-side detection: if edge session shows PINGs without finalization and a same-origin reconnect occurs with a new client-id within N seconds, translate/forward terminal event to new session when safe.
- Work with CDN/edge team to surface a close event when bfcache activates or expire upstream faster in these cases.
- Add telemetry to detect bfcache-induced zombie sessions across customers and create an automated mitigation.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: SDK hotfix shipped to CloudMuse (v0.9.5) and server-side idle-GC lowered for this customer's streams. Customer confirmed UX improvement on 2026-03-12. Engineering to schedule a full fix in sprint 42 (PR link above).
